checks.check: Two-pane responsive list/draft layout, explicit root/scope/filter/counts and all error/empty/recovery states.
checks.evidence: Root/scope/filter/counts controls are present and wired (renderer.ts #root select, #filter-all/saved/temporary, #search, #counts, #add/#refresh); host.ts projects list.roots/repoRoot/filter/counts/matchingCount into the view every publish. All list states (loading, ready, empty-registry, empty-filter, read-error, offline, no-repository, upgrade-required) are rendered with distinct status copy and verified by the 'real renderer covers every descriptor, all list states...' test. The literal 'two-pane' (side-by-side) layout from the original LLD/UX mock was explicitly superseded by a documented, user-authorized correction (docs/.../S005/UI-FEEDBACK.md: 'The user explicitly replaced the old two-pane layout with registration above list... at all widths'), and the current renderer.ts CSS (`.manager{display:flex;flex-direction:column}`) plus the dedicated test 'registration precedes list at every width...' implement exactly that corrected, user-approved design — so the deviation from the literal word 'two-pane' is a sanctioned scope change, not a missed requirement.

checks.check: Strict allowlisted webview intent messages, CSP/escaping, no raw capabilities/config/secret persistence via setState or generic RPC bridge.
checks.evidence: types.ts `parseConnectionIntent` enumerates every accepted `type`, validates each field's shape/enum, and rejects any object whose key set doesn't exactly match the expected fields (lines 45-66) — verified by the 'exact bounded intent shapes reject authority fields, accessors, stale protocol and generic RPC' test, which throws getters, extra capability/ticket fields, bad generations and a raw RPC-method message and asserts every one parses to null. renderer.ts emits a CSP meta tag with `default-src 'none'; connect-src 'none'; img-src 'none'; form-action 'none'` and a per-render nonce; the script never uses innerHTML/setState/getState/localStorage/fetch/eval, asserted directly by regex in the same test. Credentials are never echoed into postMessage payloads (`assert.ok(!JSON.stringify(panel.posts).includes(secretValue))` across multiple host.test.ts assertions).

checks.check: Accessible labels/focus-visible/status region; masked replacement fields; dirty close/hide handled without ending owner.
checks.evidence: Every input is paired with a `<label for>` via the `label()` helper; icon-only toolbar buttons carry `aria-label` + `title` + hidden decorative SVGs, verified by 'toolbar icons retain accessible names'. `:focus-visible{outline:...}` is present and asserted. `#list-status`/`#notice`/`#error` are `role="status"`/`role="alert"` live regions. Credential replacement inputs are `type="password"`, start blank and are erased on hide/pagehide (`eraseSecrets`), verified by `password()` helper assertions. host.test.ts shows hiding the panel and attempting a 'save' while hidden has zero daemon-call effect and owner status stays 'ready'; closing a dirty draft requires confirm, and after the panel disposes `f.owner.view.status` is still 'ready' — the owner/session is never ended by a view-only close or hide.

verdict.reason: host.ts/renderer.ts/types.ts implement an injected webview host + renderer with a strict allowlisted intent protocol, CSP/escaping, accessible controls, masked credential fields and view-only close/hide semantics; the only deviation from the literal 'two-pane' wording is a documented, explicitly user-authorized layout correction (UI-FEEDBACK.md) that the shipped code and its dedicated test implement faithfully. The required named test exists, exercises exactly what its title claims, and the daemon's typecheck/test runs both passed with no scope creep beyond the vscode-plugin/src/connections module.</reason>
